title.narrative: Strengthen Protection and GBV Services for Conflict-Affected Communities in Central Tigray.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project aims to respond effectively to critical protection challenges and GBV risks affecting IDPs, returnees, and host communities in the Central Zone of Tigray. Due to conflict and displacement, many vulnerable groups including women, girls, persons with disabilities, and marginalized populations face heightened exposure to protection threats such as physical violence, sexual exploitation, forced displacement, and harmful coping mechanisms that undermine their safety and dignity. The project’s overarching goal is to reduce these protection risks and provide comprehensive, survivor-centered GBV services through coordinated efforts with the General Protection and GBV clusters, local authorities, and humanitarian partners. Protection monitoring will be conducted regularly to identify and document protection risks and violations, enabling timely and evidence based responses. Vulnerability screening will help prioritize assistance to those most at risk,this intervention is designed to alleviate economic pressures that often drive negative coping mechanisms such as early or forced marriage,and exploitation, thereby promoting safer environments for women and girls. Additionally, community protection committees and local leaders will be trained and empowered to identify, refer, and prevent protection violations, fostering local ownership and sustainability of protection efforts.lt/pgtltpgtOn the GBV front, the project focuses on delivering integrated, multi-sectoral care that addresses the immediate and longer-term needs of survivors. GBV case management services will be closely linked with SRH care to ensure survivors receive timely medical treatment, psychosocial support, and protection referrals. MHPSS, including psychological first aid, will be provided to survivors and other affected community members to address trauma and promote healing. The establishment of Women and Girls Friendly Spaces will offer safe and supportive environments where survivors can access psychosocial support, empowerment activities, and receive information on GBV prevention and response. Emergency cash assistance will be available to survivors to cover transportation and other costs necessary to access specialized services, removing financial barriers to care. Furthermore, ltbrgtreusable sanitary pad will be distributed to women and girls of reproductive age, helping to maintain their dignity and health in displacement settings. Capacity building efforts will target One-Stop Centers to strengthen their ability to provide comprehensive, multisectoral GBV services and enhance referral pathways. Community awareness-raising campaigns will aim to reduce stigma around GBV, inform communities about available services and rights, and engage men and boys as allies in prevention efforts.lt/pgtltpgtThe project’s implementation will emphasize strong coordination among protection actors, health services,and local authorities to ensure comprehensive, efficient, and survivor-centered service delivery. Community engagement mechanisms will be established to facilitate feedback, promote accountability, and tailor interventions to the evolving needs of affected populations.Through these integrated protection and GBV interventions, the project seeks to enhance safety, dignity, and resilience among vulnerable populations in the Central Zone of Tigray. ltbrgtlt/pgt
